title: Deterministic cutover and surge-isolation for Hosted API deployments
creator: Maya Patel
description: Hardening the Hosted API deployment pipeline to provide deterministic cutovers across regions, isolate capacity/surge during traffic shifts, and make rollbacks reproducible. This ticket implements a new controller and operator-level rehearsals that combine blue/green cutovers with staged traffic attenuation and isolation windows to prevent cross-region capacity bleed and SLO violations during mass rollouts.
background: Recent rollouts exposed non-deterministic capacity spikes when we shifted traffic across regions and model variants. Contributing factors: transient queueing in gateway proxies, KV cache warm-up spikes, and downstream GPU contention on Dedicated pools. Existing canary percent steps are too coarse for multi-region rollouts and there is no rehearsable dry-run mode to validate cutover safety for a given release set.
proposed_solution: Introduce a Deterministic Cutover Controller (DCC) that coordinates: 1) a fast preflight simulation of target traffic percentages, 2) windowed surge-isolation where new instances are progressively unthrottled with per-region rate limits, 3) a multi-metric gate evaluating latency P95, 5xx rate, queue depth, and model-quality regression signals, and 4) an automated rollback choreography with timeboxed backoff. Expose configuration via the Console rollout page and an API flag to run 'rehearsal' mode which performs a simulated shift without impacting production backends.
acceptance_criteria:
- DCC can perform a deterministic dry-run and produce a reproducible plan for a given release and region list.
- Live rollout using DCC does staged traffic changes with surge-isolation windows configurable per-region.
- Rollouts abort and fully rollback automatically if any configured gate metric breaches threshold for >2 consecutive evaluation windows.
- Cutover does not produce >10% increase in 95th percentile latency system-wide for monitored SLOs during a normal rollout.
- Post-cutover telemetry is tagged and traceable in Console for 30 days.
- Documentation and runbook published, and at least one on-call runbook rehearsal completed.
implementation_steps:
1) Design DCC API and rollout manifest fields (region list, staged percents, isolation window ms, gate metrics).
2) Add rehearsal mode to runtime routing plane to simulate weight changes and report projected KV cache hit/warm metrics.
3) Implement surge-isolation token bucket per-region in the gateway so new instances receive a bounded ramp of traffic.
4) Wire the DCC to Console to display progress and to the existing SLO/alerting infra for gate evaluation.
5) Author automated rollback choreography and test harness that can force-abort or rollback to previous LTS model version.
6) Run synthetic validation with recorded production traces and a shadow shift in a staging region.
7) Iterate thresholds after three rehearsal runs and schedule a small-prod rollout with on-call present.
rollout_plan:
Phase A: Dry-run rehearsals in staging (2 runs across east & west staging clusters).
Phase B: Low-risk production run limited to 5% traffic in a single non-critical region for 1 hour with on-call and flighting.
Phase C: Multi-region progressive run using DCC at 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% per region with 20-minute isolation windows.
Abort conditions: any gate metric exceeds threshold for 2 evaluation windows, sustained queue depth > preflight projection, or operator manual abort.
Post-rollout: 1-hour observation then promote to full rollout if clean.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for DCC manifest parsing and simulated weight plans.
- Integration tests that run rehearsal mode against a stubbed routing plane and assert reproducible plans.
- Load test that replays production traffic and measures latency and KV cache warm-up with and without surge-isolation.
- Chaos test: introduce a slow GPU worker during a simulated cutover and assert rollback triggers.
- SLO regression test against historical baselines to ensure <10% P95 increase.
monitoring_playbook:
- Dashboards to surface per-region rollout percent, P50/P95 latencies, 5xx rate, queue depth, KV cache hit ratio, and Dedicated pool GPU utilization.
- Alert rule: RolloutGateBreached if any gate metric breaches threshold for >2 windows. Pager goes to release-engineering then on-call.
- Runbook steps: (1) DCC abort will trigger automated rollback; (2) if rollback fails, isolate region and divert traffic to fallback model variant; (3) open emergency incident and escalate to runtime and infra leads.
- Postmortem checklist includes collection of traces, kernel-level GPU metrics, and step-wise timeline from DCC logs.
notes: We should coordinate with Dedicated capacity owners to reserve burst headroom for first isolation windows. Consider temporary rate-limits on large enterprise tenants during rollout windows to avoid noisy-neighbor effects. Rehearsal mode must not mutate customer billing or metrics state.
